judgments.reasoning_cat2: This is the clearest candidate for relationship risk in the instrument. A and B state that 'any changes in the Plan Document will control the terms of this Agreement', and C reserves to County the right to 'substitute another contribution structure' which 'shall control the terms of this Agreement' - three unilateral amendment powers over Agreement terms, against Art. V sec. 14 (modification 'in writing only, signed by the parties in interest') and Art. V sec. 22 (no modification effective other than as recited). B also reduces County's stated $17,500 contribution by administrative costs, in tension with its own fixed-dollar promise. A court would likely treat the specific pension provisions as controlling over the general amendment clause, which is why I stop short of a flag.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two declaratory sentences with a specific statutory basis and a specific cut-off date (March 31, 1986). The characterisation of the Kern County Pension Plan as 'a qualified alternative to the insurance system established by the federal Social Security Act' is a legal conclusion rather than an ambiguous term, and 'Social Security taxes' versus 'Medicare taxes' are conventionally distinguished.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: There is surface friction with Art. II sec. 1.A, which has County paying 'the Employer's portion of the hospital insurance portion of Social Security ("FICA 2")' while this section declares the physician exempt from Social Security taxes. The two reconcile once 'hospital insurance' is read as the Medicare component - which is exactly why the 1986 carve-out is limited to Medicare - so the instrument hangs together: a post-1986 hire pays Medicare, County pays the employer share, and OASDI is displaced by the pension plan. Art. III sec. 5.E's exclusion from other County retirement plans is consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Eligibility benchmarked to full-time County employees in a named plan, with an express no-breach rule for plan changes. Nothing vague or double-edged.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel in form to Art. III secs. 2, 4 and 8 and subject to the same Art. V secs. 14/22 amendment-clause interaction, expressly defused by the no-breach sentence. Art. III sec. 5.E excludes other retirement plans but names the Kern County Employees' Retirement Association and retirement plans, not the Deferred Compensation Plan, so no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same clean structure as the deferred compensation clause: named plan, benchmarked eligibility ('eligible County employees'), express no-breach rule for changes. No term requiring construction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the other Article III benchmarked-benefit provisions and with Art. V secs. 14 and 22 for the reasons given there. No provision of the Agreement contradicts Kern$Flex eligibility.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mostly definite, with named caps ($2,500 per year; $20,000 moving) and a specific three-bid, lowest-bid, invoice-supported procedure. Two soft points: 'approved and necessary expenditures' appears in both A and B without saying who approves or by what standard; and A's cap sentence shifts vocabulary to 'expenses and materials not to exceed $2,500 per year', so whether the cap covers all of A's seminar fees, travel and study materials or only the narrower 'expenses and materials' is not cleanly resolved.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A imposes a $2,500 annual cap on continuing-education reimbursement while B provides uncapped reimbursement for 'education and training as directed by KMC' - a real question whether the cap is circumvented by directing the training, though the elective/directed distinction is a sound harmonisation. D and E cross-refer accurately to Art. II secs. 4 and 5. C's Philadelphia-to-Bakersfield relocation coexists with the Art. V sec. 18 notice address in Valencia, California, which is odd but not operative.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The nameable defect is 'whichever is applicable'. The clause offers two alternative review tracks - the Faculty Practice Board policy titled 'Corrective Action and Termination Review Process' and the medical staff bylaws - without any criterion for choosing between them, so the provision that is supposed to supply the procedure leaves the choice of procedure undetermined. The named policy title and the bylaws are at least specifically identified, which limits the vagueness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This section reviews and appeals 'the decision to impose corrective action or terminate for cause', but no operative provision of this instrument authorises corrective action or for-cause termination: Article IV contains only sec. 1.A, the physician's without-cause right, and sec. 2 is absent from the Agreement. The referenced decision has no source, so the appeal machinery hangs unattached - a whole-instrument gap, aggravated by Art. V sec. 13's separate immediate-termination trigger (privileges restricted) and Art. V sec. 11's reservation of concurrent cumulative remedies to County, which cuts against channelling anything through a mandatory review process. A court could still fill the gap from the medical staff bylaws incorporated by Art. V secs. 10 and 13, so I stop just short of a confident flag.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two flat prohibitions with one qualified consent carve-out: no assignment or transfer of the Agreement or its obligations 'or any part thereof', and no assignment of money due without County's prior written approval. Standard and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Art. II sec. 4.E and sec. 5.B, which let the physician or his practice group direct the Plan Administrator as to distribution of net fees - direction of distribution is not an assignment, and in any event County's written approval mechanism accommodates it. Also consistent with Art. V sec. 14's writing requirement. No conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To testify as an expert witness or otherwise' is an unbounded catch-all attached to a single specific - on its face it could reach any form of assistance in any proceeding, and the section heading ('Assistance in Litigation') is expressly stripped of interpretive force by Art. V sec. 4. There is also an internal pull between 'at no cost to County' and the following sentence crediting the time as compensated administrative time. The named-party exception is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The clause promises credit for 'administrative time as defined in the compensation plan', but Article II - the compensation plan - nowhere defines 'administrative time'; it refers only to 'administrative duties' in sec. 3.A(4) and to step-placement criteria located in an external manual. So the operative cross-reference points to a definition the instrument does not contain. It also sits beside Art. II sec. 5.A, which treats 'professional witness fees' as the physician's own other income, though sec. 2 is confined to litigation against County or KMC.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single flat negative: no authority to bind County or KMC to any agreements or undertakings, in performance of 'any and all duties under this Agreement'. Broad but unambiguous - breadth in a disclaimer of authority narrows rather than expands the interpretive question.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Some friction with Exhibit A, which makes the physician department chairman and medical director of the laboratories, reviewing 'department budgets and major expenditures' and sitting on the Medical Executive Committee and Faculty Practice Board, and with Art. II sec. 7.B's negotiation of overhead. But each of those roles is either internal review or negotiation with the CEO on County's side of the table, and none purports to confer contracting authority, so the disclaimer harmonises.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two standard interpretive directives, both definite: headings disregarded, and no contra proferentem because the Agreement is deemed jointly prepared. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It does real work elsewhere - it is what blunts a construe-against-the-drafter attack on the County-favouring provisions (Art. V sec. 11 cumulative remedies to County, sec. 17 waiver only by County's written consent), and it neutralises reliance on captions such as Article IV's 'TERMINATION AND CORRECTIVE ACTION' heading. Its 'jointly prepared' premise is reinforced rather than contradicted by Art. V sec. 20's bargaining recital. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: California law, performance in Kern County, venue in Kern County - three definite designations. No ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coherent with the parties' identities and with Art. V sec. 8's California regulatory references (Title 22, FEHA, Cal-OSHA) and Art. II sec. 3.A's Welfare and Institutions Code citation. Nothing in the instrument designates a different forum or law.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Specific statutory citations (Government Code sections 1090 et seq. and 87100 et seq.), a definite representation of present unawareness, and a definite consequence keyed to a definite time ('if such a financial interest does exist at the inception of this Agreement'). 'Financial or economic interest' is a statutory concept with developed content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This is one of the County's scattered termination rights ('County may immediately terminate this Agreement by giving written notice thereof'), which coexists uneasily with Article IV - the article captioned for termination, which confers no County termination right at all - and with Art. V sec. 13's separate immediate-termination trigger and sec. 15's 30-day non-appropriation notice. Read as cumulative under Art. V sec. 11, they can stand together; the resulting scatter is untidy rather than contradictory, and this clause's trigger is narrow and self-contained.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The obligation to comply with 'all applicable KMC and County policies and procedures' is open-ended and delegated to documents the Agreement never identifies, and the conformance list is introduced by 'including, but not limited to' - a general catch-all against enumerated specifics (orientation, case conferences, supervision, in-service education, patients' rights functions, performance improvement). Against that, the specific duties (daily time sheets on KMC forms, submission to drug and laboratory testing and physical examinations) are entirely definite, and 'applicable' supplies some limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The unbounded policy incorporation has to be read with Art. V sec. 22, whose entire-agreement clause covers only 'all attachments hereto', and with Art. V sec. 10's disclaimer of classified-employee status and Civil Service protections. It coexists with the parallel incorporations of the medical staff bylaws (secs. 10, 13, 19) and the Faculty Practice manual (Art. II sec. 3.B), so incorporation by reference is the instrument's consistent method rather than an aberration. Daily time sheets also fit Exhibit A sec. 6's 2112-hour tracking objective.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Structured general-then-specific: a general duty to comply with all applicable County, state and federal law, then 'including but not limited to' a list of named regimes (JCAHO, Title 22, EMTALA, Medi-Cal/Medicaid and Medicare billing rules, EEOC, HIPAA, FEHA, Cal-OSHA). Because the general term comes first and the list is expressly non-exhaustive, expressio unius has little purchase - the enumeration illustrates rather than limits. Definite closing licensure obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reinforces rather than disturbs the instrument: Recital C and Art. V sec. 13 on licensure, Exhibit A sec. 1.a-b on laboratory regulation and CAP/AABB accreditation, Exhibit A sec. 4.b on CMS documentation for professional fee billing, and Art. II sec. 4's billing structure. The only friction is with Art. V sec. 16's narrower enumerated discrimination list, since this section incorporates FEHA and EEOC standards that reach further.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate counterparts clause; every element (any number of counterparts, each an original, all one instrument) is settled and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits the multi-signature execution page (KMC CEO, Kern County Personnel, County Counsel, Board Chairman, physician) with its differing dates. No provision contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two definite propositions: the physician is employed by County pursuant to this Agreement and the KMC medical staff bylaws, and he is not a classified employee and has no rights under the Civil Service Ordinance, rules or regulations. 'Classified employee' is a term of art in county civil service systems; the acknowledgment form makes the intended effect plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The employee/non-classified line is drawn consistently but the instrument keeps pulling both ways around it: Art. II sec. 2.G promises defence and indemnity 'to the same extent as would be afforded to a regular full-time County employee', Article III benchmarks nearly every benefit to 'regular County employees of KMC', the preamble calls him a 'contract employee', and Recital A invokes Government Code section 31000 authority to contract with specially trained persons. These are reconcilable - benefits by benchmark, status by express disclaimer - and the loss of civil-service protections is what makes Article IV's termination gap matter, but sec. 10 itself states the position clearly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear allocation of ownership to County, then a defined access right bounded by two stated purposes (meeting professional responsibilities to the patient; assisting in the defence of a malpractice or similar claim) and by compliance with legal requirements and confidentiality standards. 'Or similar claim' is a small catch-all but tethered to the specific it follows.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Art. V sec. 8 (HIPAA compliance), sec. 2 (assistance in litigation) and Art. II sec. 4 (billing records maintained by the billing service and accounted to the Plan Administrator). County ownership of records does not collide with any other provision I could find.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The credentialing checklist (a)-(d) is definite. The defect-prone sentence is 'This Agreement may be immediately terminated if Core Physician's privileges/membership are modified or restricted' - drafted in the passive with no actor named, so who may terminate is left unstated, and 'modified or restricted ... such that services performed by Core Physician are limited or restricted' sets a threshold without a measure of materiality (any limitation, or one that defeats performance?).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This is a County termination right located outside Article IV, the article captioned 'TERMINATION AND CORRECTIVE ACTION', whose sec. 1 confers a termination right only on the physician and whose sec. 2 is missing. It operates immediately and without notice, unlike sec. 15's 30 days and Art. IV sec. 1.A's 90 days, and its trigger - bylaws action restricting privileges - is the very kind of decision Art. IV sec. 3 subjects to a review and appeal process, so termination could precede the appeal it presupposes. Art. V sec. 11's cumulative-remedies clause supports coexistence, which keeps this below a confident flag.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One short sentence, entirely definite as to form (writing) and signatories (the parties in interest at the time of the modification). Nothing ambiguous to name.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The exclusivity of 'in writing only' is difficult to square with several provisions that let one side change Agreement terms unilaterally: Art. III secs. 5.A and 5.B ('any changes in the Plan Document will control the terms of this Agreement') and sec. 5.C (a County-substituted contribution structure 'shall control the terms of this Agreement'), plus Art. II sec. 2.F(1)'s annually Board-set assessment on compensation. The benchmarked-benefit clauses (Art. III secs. 2, 3.A, 4, 7, 8) are drafted to avoid the clash by stipulating that changes are 'not a breach', and the specific pension provisions would likely be held to control over this general clause - but the instrument does contain competing amendment mechanics, and Art. II sec. 1.C's written-amendment requirement for compensation only sharpens the contrast.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The notice period (30 days) and the carve-outs (services performed before termination; liability for existing default) are definite. The trigger is oddly constructed: termination is available where 'insufficient funds are appropriated or budgeted for this Agreement in any fiscal year due to closing of a clinical department or KMC' - the causal link runs from a closure to the non-appropriation, so it is unclear whether a plain funding shortfall without a closure suffices, or a closure without a shortfall. That is a nameable scope question, though the conjunction of both conditions is the more natural reading.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Another County termination right sitting outside Article IV, on a third notice period (30 days, against Art. IV sec. 1.A's 90 days and secs. 6 and 13's immediate termination), and cutting against Art. I sec. 1's fixed term through October 4, 2007. Non-appropriation clauses are conventional in public contracts and Art. V sec. 11 permits cumulative remedies, so the coexistence is workable; the release of 'any further financial obligation' also fits Art. II sec. 1.A's maximum-payable framing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: This is a genuine general-versus-specific problem. The first sentence agrees to abide by 'all laws, federal, state and local, and by all policies of the County of Kern respecting discrimination'; the second then enumerates a closed list of protected characteristics - 'race, color, national origin, age, religion, marital status or sexual preference' - with no 'including' or 'not limited to'. The enumeration conspicuously omits sex, disability, medical condition and pregnancy, all covered by the very statutes the Agreement elsewhere adopts, so expressio unius invites the argument that the parties' own non-discrimination covenant is narrower than the general sentence preceding it. Whether the closed list qualifies or merely illustrates the general duty is left unresolved on the face of the clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The narrow list pulls against Art. V sec. 8, which obliges the physician to comply with 'EEOC, HIPAA, FEHA' among other regimes - FEHA and Title VII reach sex, disability and medical condition, characteristics the sec. 16 list drops - and against sec. 16's own first sentence incorporating all County anti-discrimination policies. A court would probably harmonise by treating the general sentence as controlling and the list as illustrative, which keeps this from being an irreconcilable conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite in operation: waiver only by County's written consent, forbearance or indulgence is not waiver, and County may still invoke any remedy. 'Forbearance or indulgence by County in any regard whatsoever' is broad but its breadth is the point and creates no competing meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Wholly one-directional - it addresses only waiver of covenants 'to be performed by Core Physician' and says nothing about waiver of County's obligations - which pairs with Art. V sec. 11's County-only cumulative remedies. Art. V sec. 4's no-contra-proferentem rule and sec. 20's bargaining recital are the instrument's answer to that asymmetry. Consistent with sec. 14's writing requirement; no contradiction found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Exhaustively mechanical: three permitted delivery methods, a deemed-receipt rule for each (personal on receipt; mailed or expressed four days after deposit), named addressees with street addresses, and a self-executing address-change procedure. No vague term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplies the machinery the notice-dependent provisions need - Art. IV sec. 1.A (90 days), Art. V sec. 15 (30 days), secs. 6 and 13 (immediate termination on written notice), Art. II sec. 1.C. The only oddity is that the physician's notice address is in Valencia while Art. III sec. 9.C funds relocation from Philadelphia to Bakersfield, but the address-change mechanism absorbs that.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The standard of performance is expressed in evaluative terms - 'diligent and conscientious manner' and 'accepted professional and ethical standards of the medical profession' - which are imprecise on their face. But they are conventional professional-services standards with established content, and the clause anchors them to an identified external source (the medical staff bylaws of KMC), so the boundary is ascertainable by expert evidence rather than genuinely indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Dovetails with Art. I sec. 2 and Exhibit A (the services and duties), Art. V secs. 10 and 13 (bylaws governance), and Art. V sec. 8 (regulatory compliance). Nothing in the instrument sets a competing performance standard.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A recital-style acknowledgment: specialized professional services, mutual legal knowledge and skill, arm's-length bargaining, opportunity to review. It creates no obligation whose boundary needs to be located, so vagueness has nothing to attach to.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Serves the same function as Art. V sec. 4's jointly-prepared rule and sec. 22's entire-agreement clause - a coherent trio directed at foreclosing construe-against-the-drafter and extrinsic-inducement arguments. Its 'specialized, professional services' framing echoes Recital A's section 31000 language while Art. V sec. 10 makes him an employee, but sec. 20 does not itself characterise the status.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard severability with a conventional proviso ('provided such remaining portions or provisions can be construed in substance to constitute the agreement which the parties intended to enter into in the first instance'). The proviso requires judgment but is the settled formulation; no term carries two competing meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A gap-filler that supports rather than disturbs the instrument, and it interacts sensibly with Art. III sec. 5.C (substitute pension structure if the IRS withholds a favourable determination) and Art. V sec. 8's compliance obligations. No provision contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conventional integration language, definite in each limb: the Agreement and all attachments are the entire agreement; no inducements, representations or promises other than those recited; no oral promise, modification, change or inducement effective. The qualifier 'relating to the services, rights, obligations and covenants contained herein' narrows the clause somewhat but does so in identifiable terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The integration extends only to 'all attachments hereto', yet the Agreement's substance depends on several unattached external documents - the KMC Faculty Practice Administrative Policies and Procedures Manual (Art. II sec. 3.B(1)-(3)), the Plan Document (Art. III sec. 5), the medical staff bylaws (Art. V secs. 10, 13, 19), the Faculty Practice Board policy named in Art. IV sec. 3 and County personnel policies (Art. V sec. 7). Art. III sec. 5's statement that changes in the Plan Document 'will control the terms of this Agreement' is in particular tension with 'no oral promise, modification, change or inducement shall be effective'. The example instrument's entire-agreement clause was held clean despite comparable friction, and incorporation by reference is a recognised harmonisation, so I keep this below the flag.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three definite propositions: the chairman serves as medical director for anatomic pathology and the clinical laboratories, reports to the KMC Medical Director, and the position is full-time 'requiring 48 hours of service, on average, per week'. The 'on average' qualifier is expressly reconciled by Exhibit A sec. 6. No ambiguous term to name.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The number is the problem in context: Exhibit A fixes the commitment at 48 hours per week, while Art. II sec. 1.A - the clause that pays for the commitment - defines full-time as 'according to AMA survey data for specialty but no less than forty [40] hours per week'. Whether the compensated full-time obligation is 40 or 48 hours is therefore not settled by the instrument, and Art. I sec. 2 incorporates Exhibit A without a priority rule (there is no order-of-precedence clause anywhere). The floor language 'no less than 40' supplies a workable harmonisation, and Exhibit A sec. 5's 'other duties as assigned' by 'the chief executive officer or medical director' slightly muddies the single reporting line stated here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Items a-c are anchored to identifiable external standards (federal and state clinical laboratory regulations; CAP and AABB accreditation; KMC policies and the medical staff bylaws) and are definite by reference. Item d is not: 'Operates effectively and smoothly, and provides timely reports, provided adequate resources are provided' stacks three evaluative terms with no measure - 'effectively and smoothly', 'timely', and an express condition turning on 'adequate resources' with no standard for adequacy and no statement of who must supply them. Since d is a performance obligation whose breach could support corrective action, the vagueness is operative rather than cosmetic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Art. V sec. 8 (JCAHO, Title 22 compliance), sec. 7 (KMC policies), sec. 19 (professional standards) and Exhibit A sec. 2's more granular duties. Item d's 'adequate resources' proviso has no counterpart obligation anywhere in the Agreement requiring County to furnish resources - a gap rather than a contradiction, and the general Art. V secs. 11/17 framework leaves the condition's effect to ordinary construction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Fourteen duties, most of them concrete and checkable (named committees, monthly meetings with the medical director, CAP proficiency surveys, annual evaluations, annual department report). Two open ends: g closes a list of six named committees with 'and other committees that may be assigned by the president of the medical staff', and n reads 'Completes clinical pathology and anatomic pathology service work as may be required' without saying by whom or how much. Both catch-alls are bounded by an assignment mechanism or by the department's evident scope, which limits the ejusdem generis exposure; d's 'timely manner' and e's 'appropriateness' are evaluative but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coherent with the rest of the instrument: g's Faculty Practice Board membership matches Art. II sec. 2.E, b and d match Art. V sec. 7's performance-improvement duties, and n aligns with Exhibit A sec. 4's patient-care duties and Art. II sec. 3.A's teaching and administrative components of base salary. The volume of administrative and committee work sits in some tension with Art. II sec. 1.A's 40-hour full-time floor and Exhibit A sec. 6's 2112-hour objective, but the duties are cumulative with, not contrary to, those provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three concrete teaching duties, with the conferences actually named (weekly gynecology, oncology, surgery) and the activities specified (didactic lectures; departmental, interdepartmental and interdisciplinary programs). 'Actively participates' is evaluative but minor, and 'to include' introduces a list that is plainly illustrative of an identified activity rather than a catch-all doing independent work.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Art. II sec. 3.A(3), which makes teaching a component of base salary, and Exhibit A secs. 2.k and 2.m on resident training and educational conferences. Art. III sec. 3.D's education leave concerns the physician's own education, not these duties. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Very short. 'Performs anatomic pathology services as assigned' leaves both the assignor and the volume unstated, which is a real if modest indefiniteness for the clause that defines the clinical component of a physician's job; b, by contrast, is precise ('consistent with CMS requirements for professional fee billing'). The 'as assigned' formulation is standard in job descriptions and readable against Exhibit A's reporting line to the KMC Medical Director.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits Art. II sec. 4 (professional fees from 'direct patient care', billing and documentation), Art. II sec. 3.A(1)-(2) (base salary covers indigent, incarcerated and under-compensated patient care) and Exhibit A sec. 2.n. That the patient-care duties are the shortest item in a job description dominated by administrative duties creates a mild tension with a compensation plan built on professional fee generation, but nothing contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: This is the general-versus-specific pattern in its purest form: after four sections of carefully enumerated administrative, teaching and patient-care duties, the Exhibit closes with an unqualified 'Other duties as assigned by the chief executive officer or medical director' - a catch-all whose outer reach is fixed by nothing except the assignor's discretion. Its scope is genuinely contestable (does it reach duties of a different kind from those enumerated, or only cognate ones?), and because Art. I sec. 2 makes Exhibit A the measure of the physician's obligations, the indeterminacy is operative. The identification of the two officers who may assign is what keeps it from being wholly open-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit A's introduction states a single reporting line - 'The pathology chairman will report to the KMC Medical Director' - while this item empowers both the chief executive officer and the medical director to assign duties; a minor inconsistency in lines of authority, mitigated by Art. II sec. 3.A(5) ('other activities approved by the CEO of KMC and the Faculty Practice Board') which likewise contemplates CEO involvement. Unlimited additional duties also press against Art. II sec. 1.A's fixed compensation and 40-hour floor and Exhibit A sec. 6's 2112-hour objective, but ejusdem generis rather than a conflict rule is the natural control.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Quantified and self-reconciling: a 48-hour standard workweek, express acknowledgment that actual hours may vary week to week with assignments, and a measurable annual target of 2112 worked hours. The word 'objective' leaves it slightly unclear whether 2112 hours is a binding obligation or an aspiration, but the sentence structure makes 48 hours the standard and 2112 the annualised expression of it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The hours figure conflicts in appearance with Art. II sec. 1.A, which pays for full-time work 'according to AMA survey data for specialty but no less than forty [40] hours per week' - 40 versus 48, with no order-of-precedence clause to resolve Exhibit A against the body. On the arithmetic the Exhibit is coherent with Article III: 2112 hours is 44 weeks at 48 hours, leaving roughly the 384 hours of vacation (160), sick leave (64), education leave (80) and holidays that Art. III sec. 3 provides. That consistency, plus the 'no less than 40' floor, supports harmonisation, so I stop below the flag.
